subtitle: A Greek Envoy’s Vow beneath the Garuda Standard

panels.shot: low-angle wide of an ancient pillar rising against the sky, with Heliodorus in partial silhouette at its base
panels.action: Heliodorus stands before a freshly raised stone pillar crowned with a stylized Garuda figure, dry central Indian plains and a distant Shunga-era town behind him under a blazing sun.

dialogue.text: In Shunga India, a Greek envoy from Taxila raised a Garuda pillar to Vasudeva—and carved into stone that devotion could cross borders.

i18n.hi: शुंग भारत में, तक्षशिला का एक यूनानी दूत वासुदेव के लिए गरुड़ स्तंभ खड़ा करता है—पत्थर पर उकेर देता है कि भक्ति सरहदों से आगे जाती है।

panels.shot: close-up on weathered stone inscription, camera tight on Brahmi letters carved into the pillar
panels.action: The frame lingers on the pillar’s midsection where crisp Brahmi characters name Heliodorus, the son of Dion, with Heliodorus’ hand hovering near the carved lines.

dialogue.text: On this pillar at Besnagar, the stone still reads: Heliodorus, son of Dion, a man of Taxila, envoy of King Antialcidas, a Bhagavata, set up this Garuda-standard for Vasudeva.

i18n.hi: इस बेसनगर स्तंभ पर आज भी लिखा है: हेलियोदोरस, दियोन का पुत्र, तक्षशिला का पुरुष, राजा अन्तियाल्किदास का दूत, एक भागवत, ने यह गरुड़-ध्वज वासुदेव के लिए स्थापित किया।

panels.shot: wide bird’s-eye shot of the subcontinent with routes traced, then push-in towards the northwest
panels.action: A map-like vista shows the northwestern frontier lands, the city of Taxila nestled amid hills, caravan routes leading east toward the Ganges plain, and distant central India shimmering on the horizon.

dialogue.text: To reach this stone, Heliodorus first came from the northwest—from Greek-ruled Taxila, where Indo-Greek kings watched the Indian plains with hungry and curious eyes.

i18n.hi: इस पत्थर तक पहुँचने के लिए हेलियोदोरस उत्तर-पश्चिम से चला—यूनानी शासित तक्षशिला से, जहाँ इंडो-यूनानी राजा भूखी, जिज्ञासु आँखों से भारतीय मैदानों को ताकते थे।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a Hellenistic-style hall in Taxila, angled to show Indo-Greek and local elements together
panels.action: Heliodorus stands in a colonnaded hall adorned with Greek motifs and local patterns, listening intently as an Indo-Greek king in diadem and Indian dress leans from a low throne, attendants in mixed garb nearby.

dialogue.text: His king, Antialcidas, ruled a patchwork of peoples—Bactrian Greeks, Gandharan traders, Indian towns—and needed more than soldiers: he needed envoys who could move between worlds.

i18n.hi: उसका राजा अन्तियाल्किदास टुकड़ों का राज्य चलाता था—बैक्ट्रियन यूनानी, गांधार के व्यापारी, भारतीय नगर—और उसे सिर्फ सैनिक नहीं, ऐसे दूत चाहिए थे जो दुनियाएँ पार कर सकें।

panels.shot: two-shot, oblique angle, focusing on the king leaning forward and Heliodorus in attentive profile
panels.action: Antialcidas gestures toward a painted map showing the central Indian plateau and the name of the Shunga ruler, while Heliodorus stands straight, hand over chest, absorbing instructions.

dialogue.speaker: heliodorus
dialogue.text: I will go to the Shunga court and return with friendship, Basileus.

i18n.hi: मैं शुंग दरबार जाऊँगा, और मैत्री लेकर लौटूँगा, बसिलेवस।

panels.shot: long tracking wide along a caravan moving across rugged terrain
panels.action: Heliodorus rides with a caravan of pack animals and mixed escorts across rocky passes and dusty plains, Hellenistic helmets and Indian turbans mingling under a harsh sun.

dialogue.text: From Taxila, he followed the old trade roads: past hill shrines and river ferries, through towns where Greek coin met Indian measure and many gods shared the same sky.

i18n.hi: तक्षशिला से वह पुरानी व्यापार राहों पर चला: पहाड़ी देवालयों और नदी घाटों के पार, उन कस्बों से जहाँ यूनानी सिक्का भारतीय बाट से मिलता और कई देव एक ही आकाश बाँटते।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Vidisha/Besnagar region with fortifications and temples
panels.action: The camera reveals the lush environs near the confluence of rivers by Vidisha and Besnagar, with earthen ramparts, wooden halls, tiled roofs, and temple spires rising above groves of trees.

dialogue.text: Heliodorus came at last to the central Indian heartland—Vidisha and nearby Besnagar—where Shunga power watched the highways and shrines drew pilgrims to Vasudeva.

i18n.hi: आख़िर हेलियोदोरस मध्य भारत के हृदय में पहुँचा—विदिशा और पास के बेसनगर—जहाँ शुंग शक्ति मार्गों को ताँकती, और वासुदेव के तीर्थ यात्रियों से भरते।

panels.shot: medium shot in a Shunga audience hall, slight low angle, crowded with courtiers
panels.action: In a timber-pillared hall, Heliodorus bows before a Shunga king—Bhagabhadra—who sits on a low platform with Brahmin advisers and armed guards, all studying the foreign envoy carefully.

dialogue.text: At the Shunga court of Bhagabhadra, the Greek from Taxila was measured, word by word, gesture by gesture, as an emissary of a rival yet useful power.

i18n.hi: भगभद्र के शुंग दरबार में, तक्षशिला का यह यूनानी शब्द–शब्द, हाव–भाव से तौला गया—एक प्रतिद्वन्द्वी पर फिर भी उपयोगी शक्ति के दूत के रूप में।

panels.shot: close medium on Heliodorus speaking, with Shunga king and counselor blurred in foreground
panels.action: Heliodorus, calm and dignified, speaks with open hands while the Shunga king listens, a Brahmin counselor leaning in, their faces attentive but cautious.

dialogue.speaker: heliodorus
dialogue.text: My king seeks peace on these roads and trade between our lands, Maharaja.

i18n.hi: मेरे राजा को इन मार्गों पर शान्ति चाहिए, और हमारे देशों के बीच व्यापार, महाराज।

panels.shot: wide shot of a temple courtyard under construction, with artisans and priests
panels.action: Heliodorus stands at the edge of a lively temple complex where artisans carve stone, priests tend a sanctum, and a standard bearing a bird emblem is being fashioned in a dusty courtyard.

dialogue.text: Beyond the court, he saw another power: a growing shrine to Vasudeva, where priests recited, donors gave, and a new kind of devotion took firm shape in stone.

i18n.hi: दरबार से बाहर उसने दूसरी शक्ति देखी: उभरता वासुदेव मंदिर, जहाँ पुरोहित गाते, दानी देते, और भक्ति की नई धारा पत्थर में रूप लेती।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Heliodorus in profile watching a ritual, warm temple light on his face
panels.action: By the temple firelight, Heliodorus watches a ritual to Vasudeva, smoke curling up as devotees stand with folded hands, his eyes reflecting the flames and carved images.

dialogue.text: Different names, different songs—yet the same hunger for the divine.

i18n.hi: नाम भिन्न, गीत भिन्न—पर दैवी के लिए वही प्यास।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot of Heliodorus seated with a learned Brahmin under a tree
panels.action: Heliodorus sits cross-legged opposite an elderly Brahmin teacher under a spreading tree, palm-leaf manuscripts between them, as they speak quietly in the fading light.

dialogue.text: He asked, and he listened. Men like him had heard of Zeus and Apollo; now he learned of Vasudeva—of a lord who guarded devotees and accepted the faithful from many lands.

i18n.hi: वह पूछता रहा, और सुनता रहा। उसके जैसे लोग ज़्यूस और अपोलो के नाम जानते थे; अब वह वासुदेव को जान रहा था—ऐसे स्वामी को जो भक्तों की रक्षा करे और दूर–दराज़ से आए श्रद्धालुओं को अपनाए।

panels.shot: medium shot in a royal chamber, Heliodorus and the Shunga king facing each other
panels.action: Heliodorus addresses Bhagabhadra in a more informal chamber, gesturing toward a sketch of a pillar with a Garuda on top, while the king strokes his beard, considering.

dialogue.speaker: heliodorus
dialogue.text: Let there stand here a pillar, Maharaja—a standard for Vasudeva, from your friend Antialcidas’ envoy.

i18n.hi: यहाँ एक स्तंभ उठने दें, महाराज—वासुदेव का ध्वज, आपके मित्र अन्तियाल्किदास के दूत की ओर से।

panels.shot: low-angle medium on Bhagabhadra, thoughtful, with attendants behind
panels.action: Bhagabhadra leans back, eyes narrowing in thought, priests and officials watching, some cautious, some intrigued, as he weighs the offer of a foreigner dedicating to their god.

dialogue.text: A foreigner pledging loyalty to their deity, in their land. The king understood its weight: a sign to his own people and to the Indo-Greek world.

i18n.hi: एक परदेसी, उनके देवता, उनकी धरती पर निष्ठा की शपथ ले रहा था। राजा ने इसकी गहराई समझी: अपने लोगों के लिए भी संकेत, और इंडो–यूनानी जगत के लिए भी।

panels.shot: wide shot of stonecutters and artisans shaping the pillar in a yard
panels.action: Artisans chisel a tall stone shaft, others carve a stylized Garuda figure, while Heliodorus oversees with a craftsman, the Shunga emblem of authority visible on a nearby banner.

dialogue.text: Under Shunga protection, local craftsmen shaped the stone. The pillar was Indian in form, but its patron was a Greek envoy, tying his name to this god and this soil.

i18n.hi: शुंग संरक्षण में, स्थानीय शिल्पियों ने पत्थर को गढ़ा। स्तंभ रूप में भारतीय था, पर उसका यजमान यूनानी दूत—अपना नाम इस देवता और इस मिट्टी से जोड़ता हुआ।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of the pillar being hoisted upright with ropes and wooden frames
panels.action: A crowd strains on ropes as the heavy pillar, capped with the Garuda, is pulled upright with wooden scaffolding, Heliodorus guiding and priests watching solemnly.

dialogue.text: One morning, with ropes and chants, the pillar rose. The Garuda emblem looked over Besnagar, as if watching the roads where kings and caravans moved.

i18n.hi: एक सुबह, रस्सों और मंत्रों के बीच स्तंभ उठा। गरुड़ चिह्न बेसनगर पर नज़र डालता, मानो उन राहों को देख रहा हो जहाँ राजा और काफ़िले चलते।

panels.shot: tight close-up on chisel striking stone, chips flying, then slight pull back
panels.action: A mason’s hand, guided by a Brahmin and Heliodorus, carves Brahmi letters into the smooth shaft; small flakes of stone leap away at each deliberate stroke.

dialogue.text: Then came the words. In Brahmi script, they named Heliodorus, son of Dion, of Taxila, envoy of Antialcidas—and they called him a Bhagavata, a devotee of Vasudeva.

i18n.hi: फिर आए शब्द। ब्राह्मी लिपि में लिखा गया: हेलियोदोरस, दियोन का पुत्र, तक्षशिला का, अन्तियाल्किदास का दूत—और उसे भागवत कहा गया, वासुदेव का भक्त।

panels.shot: medium shot of Heliodorus touching the pillar, with priests performing a ritual nearby
panels.action: Heliodorus stands with one hand resting on the pillar, eyes closed in concentration, while priests pour water and offer flowers at its base, devotees gathering quietly around.

dialogue.text: What did this mean? The stone does not say. Scholars see many possibilities: personal conversion, diplomatic devotion, or a bridge built for both politics and faith.

i18n.hi: इसका अर्थ क्या था? पत्थर चुप है। विद्वान कई रूप देखते हैं: निजी रूपांतरण, कूटनीतिक भक्ति, या राजनीति और श्रद्धा के बीच खड़ा पुल।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Heliodorus’ face in three-quarter view, serene yet resolute
panels.action: Heliodorus looks up at the Garuda, a faint, calm smile on his face, dust and incense smoke drifting between him and the towering stone.

dialogue.speaker: heliodorus
dialogue.text: Let my name stand here—as one who honored this lord in this land.

i18n.hi: मेरा नाम यहीं रहे—उसके रूप में जिसने इस देवता को, इस धरती पर, सम्मान दिया।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide of the pillar enduring seasons, from bright day to storm and dusk
panels.action: The pillar stands unchanged while villagers, pilgrims, merchants, and later ruins and fields slowly change around it, clouds racing overhead through sun, rain, and shadow.

dialogue.text: Antialcidas’ kingdom faded. The Shungas gave way. Yet the pillar remained, a quiet witness that, in one generation, a Greek envoy chose to bind himself to an Indian god.

i18n.hi: अन्तियाल्किदास का राज्य मिट गया। शुंग भी चला गया। पर स्तंभ रह गया—शांत साक्षी कि एक पीढ़ी में एक यूनानी दूत ने खुद को एक भारतीय देव से बाँधना चुना।

panels.shot: modern-era archaeologist’s-eye low close-up of the worn inscription, fingers gently tracing letters
panels.action: Modern-looking hands, dusty from excavation, gently trace the worn Brahmi letters on the weathered shaft, a measuring rod and notebook lying nearby at the base.

dialogue.text: When scholars uncovered and read these lines, they found no proclamation of conquest—but a self-chosen belonging: Heliodorus of Taxila, a foreigner, calling himself a Bhagavata of Vasudeva.

i18n.hi: जब विद्वानों ने ये पंक्तियाँ खोदकर पढ़ीं, उन्हें किसी विजय घोष का नहीं, बल्कि अपने चुने हुए अपनत्व का बयान मिला: तक्षशिला का हेलियोदोरस, परदेसी, खुद को वासुदेव का भागवत कहता हुआ।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of the pillar at sunset with a faint superimposed silhouette of Heliodorus
panels.action: At sunset, the Garuda pillar stands outlined against an orange sky, and in the foreground a faint translucent image of Heliodorus’ profile looks on, as if remembered by the stone.

dialogue.text: His story reminds us that in ancient India, as now, identity was not only inherited; it could be chosen—etched in stone by the reverence one freely offered beyond language and ancestry.

i18n.hi: उसकी कथा बताती है कि प्राचीन भारत में भी, जैसे आज, पहचान केवल विरासत नहीं थी; उसे चुना भी जा सकता था—भाषा और वंश से परे, अपनी स्वेच्छा की श्रद्धा को पत्थर पर उकेरकर।

subtitle_i18n.en: A Greek Envoy’s Vow beneath the Garuda Standard
subtitle_i18n.hi: गरुड़ ध्वज तले यूनानी दूत की प्रतिज्ञा
